key_insight: RLVR can induce unbounded language drift in chain-of-thought outputs, especially on novel reasoning tasks, whereas supervised fine-tuning does not.
engineering_relevance: For deploying and monitoring reasoning LLMs, improving CoT interpretability under RLVR may require accepting some reduction in reward or task performance.
method: Theoretical proof that RLVR optimization pressure permits unbounded language drift.
Theoretical contrast showing supervised fine-tuning does not create the same drift pressure.
Empirical analysis showing drift emerges when RLVR targets novel reasoning behaviors not already present in the base model.
evidence_signal: The paper combines formal proofs with empirical RLVR experiments on novel reasoning tasks to link drift to the difficulty of eliciting the target behavior from the base model.
watch_item: Attempts to constrain language drift may inherently constrain expected reward, so monitorability interventions could trade off against model performance.
paper_title: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training
